annotations.text: Today a part starts from a Catalog Part pick, the first field on the screen. An inventory part cannot exist unless a matching catalog entry already does.

Description first, then Part Number. Both are free text (S7-R1). No Part Library selector and no lookup step (S7-R2).

Inventory Tracking sits below the cost, Sell Price and Core Charge fields and above Tags, with the switch on by default (S4-R1, S4-R2). Min and Max sit under the switch (S4-R4).

Every empty required field shows its own error at the same time: "Description is a required field" and "Part number is a required field" (S7-N1, S7-N2). Category and Cost are required, as they are today.
The user types SLACK ADJUSTER LEFT and F40010212. F40010212 already exists in the Part Library as "Slack Adjuster", stocked at Lethbridge and not at this location.

Exactly one Part Library entry has the number typed, so the new part links to it (S7-R4, S7-R5). The entry keeps its own description (S7-R6).

The descriptions differ, so the toast reads: "Part created. Linked to F40010212 in the Part Library. Its description "Slack Adjuster" was kept." (S7-R9). There is no toast when they match, or when a new entry is created (S7-R10).

Typing f40010212 at a location that already stocks F40010212 is refused with "F40010212 already exists at this location." (S7-N3). Upper and lower case, hyphens, asterisks, periods and spaces are ignored, and the message names the number of the part already there (S7-N5).

The second line, "Please try to resolve this.", is the caption every error toast in the app carries.

With the switch off, Min and Max are hidden (S4-R5). The bin location section stays visible and is optional, so a bin can be set as a shelf reference (S4-R6).

Saving a part with tracking off also needs the Delete permission (Story 8).

CREATE A PART

A parts manager adds a part by typing its description and part number. No Part Library pick, no lookup step. Read left to right.

Board 1.0 is today's part dialog, traced from staging. Boards 1.1 to 1.6 are screenshots of the build, on Staging Heavy Duty data.
Part History records counts, transfers and field edits today. It does not say which location a change came from.
Edit Inventory Part for FF5507, "Fuel FIlter, Mack/Volvo". The Active badge sits in the title row (Story 13).

Description becomes "Fuel Filter, Mack/Volvo" and Part Number becomes FF5507A.

Lethbridge stocks the same Part Library entry, so each field says so under it: "This also changes the description at 1 other location." (S13-R12) and "This also changes the part number at 1 other location." (S13-R16). Each message shows only while the value differs from the saved one (S13-R17).
The same part is renamed in place. It keeps its stock, its bins and its history.
A "Description updated" entry and a "Part number updated" entry, each with the original and the new value, each ending "| Changed at: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919".
At Lethbridge the same part now reads FF5507A, "Fuel Filter, Mack/Volvo". Only the Create & Edit permission is needed, even though the change reaches another location (S8-R11).
The entries are written at Lethbridge too. They end with "| Changed at: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919", naming the location where the change was made (S10-R25).

CORRECT A PART'S NUMBER OR DESCRIPTION

FF5507 is stocked at Heavy Duty and at Lethbridge, with a typo in its description ("FIlter"). At Heavy Duty the user fixes the description and changes the number. Read left to right: the edit, the warnings, the list, then Part History here and at the other location.

Board 2.0 is today's Part History, traced from staging.
Today the only way to take a part out of daily work is Delete.
Part Status, Active or Inactive, sits under Part Number. The badge in the title row shows the saved status (Story 13).
Picking a status applies nothing yet. The badge keeps showing the saved status until the change is confirmed.

Save raises "Deactivate part?" (S10-R1, S10-R3). It opens with the part number and description (S10-R4), then the three lines of S10-R6, then the optional note (S10-R10). The note here reads "Superseded by N6801-06-04X".

The red Deactivate button has Cancel to its left (S10-R11). The bulk confirmation (board 4.4) is the same dialog, built from the design system Modal and Button.
Every change in the dialog is saved, the status is applied, and the dialog closes with "Part deactivated." (S13-R22). The part leaves the Active tab.
The part is listed on the Inactive tab, which lists only parts that are inactive at this location (S1-R4).
The badge reads Inactive and Part Status is on Inactive (S9-R14).
Active picked, then Save: "Activate part?", the part, then "This part can be added to new work again." and nothing more (S10-R7). The Activate button is blue (S10-R11).
Typing "superseded" in the Part History search returns the Deactivated entries whose note contains it (S10-R27). The search reads the Event text as shown and the Staff name, for every kind of entry.

RETIRE ONE PART

One part is set inactive from its own dialog, then brought back the same way. Read left to right.

Board 3.0 is today's part dialog, traced from staging. It has no status control.
No Active and Inactive tabs, no checkboxes, and no way to change many parts at once.
"Deactivate parts" sits between Cycle count and Export while the Active tab shows (S2-R1, S2-R2). A user without the Delete permission does not see it (S8-R3).

A checkbox column appears at the left (S2-R4). The bulk bar spans the list under the tabs, and the search and filter row moves under it (S2-R7). The bar shows the count, "selected" and the Deactivate button, disabled until a row is ticked (S2-R7b, S2-R8).
A click anywhere on a row ticks it instead of opening the part (S2-R5). The count reads 2.
"Deactivate parts?", "2 parts selected.", then the three lines of S10-R5 and the optional note. The Deactivate button is red (S10-R11).
"2 parts updated." (S10-R12). The parts leave the Active tab without a page reload, the mode ends and the selection clears (S2-R12, S2-R14).
On the Inactive tab the menu entry reads "Activate parts" and turns on the same mode (S3-R1). The bar button reads Activate (S3-R2). The header checkbox ticks every loaded row (S2-R6).

"Activate parts?", "2 parts selected.", "These parts can be added to new work again." and "Existing records that use them stay as they are." (S10-R8). The Activate button is blue. On confirm the parts leave the Inactive tab (S3-R4).
While bulk status mode is on, the actions menu offers only Export. Cycle count and the bulk entry come back when the mode ends (S2-R10b, S2-E4).
One change takes at most 200 parts. Here the header checkbox ticked the 630 rows loaded so far (S2-R6), so Deactivate is disabled and hovering it shows "Select 200 parts or fewer." (S2-R8a).
At a location with no inactive parts, with nothing narrowing the list, the Inactive tab says "No inactive parts at this location." (S1-N1). Shown at Staging Lethbridge.

RETIRE OR BRING BACK PARTS IN BULK

Bulk status is a mode, turned on from the actions menu the same way as Cycle count. Two parts are deactivated, then brought back from the Inactive tab. Read left to right.

Board 4.0 is today's Inventory list, traced from staging. It has no bulk status.
Hovering the info icon shows "Tracked parts keep a stock count, with Min and Max. Turn this off for items you don't count." (S4-R3).

Min and Max are hidden in the part dialog, and no bin quantity changes (S5-R3). The bin and its quantity stay visible as a shelf reference (S5-R3a). There is no confirmation, whatever the part holds (S5-R5). The change applies on Save (S5-R2).

Total Quantity reads "Not Tracked" instead of a quantity (S4-R8). Bin Location / Quantity still shows MZH1C with its 10 (S4-R8a), and Min and Max still show the saved values (S4-R8b). The Inventory Value report leaves the part out (S4-R9).

Typing "not tracked" in the Inventory search returns the untracked parts (S6-R1). When the list is sorted on Total Quantity, untracked parts sit below every tracked part in both directions (S6-R3 to S6-R7). This board shows the search only.
Turning tracking off writes "Tracking turned off", and turning it on writes "Tracking turned on" (S10-R22).
Min and Max show again with the values they had (S5-R4), and the count shows as it stands (S5-R6).
In Cycle count the untracked part shows "Not Tracked" in the Count column instead of a count box, and is never counted (S5-R12). The printed count sheet leaves it out (S5-R13).

STOP COUNTING A PART

The shop stops keeping a stock count for a part it does not count, here a winch strap. Read left to right: the switch, the list, finding untracked parts, Part History, turning it back on, then how Cycle count treats an untracked part.

There is no before board: the part dialog on staging has no tracking switch.
Today the lookup offers every part stocked at the location.
New Part Request on work order S2-9647. Typing GREASE finds GREASETUBE, as an inventory part and as its Part Library entry.
The same search returns "No results" (S9-R1). Work orders, estimates, technician charge-out, part sales and purchase orders share this lookup (S9-R1 to S9-R8).

Typing greasetube in full does not offer it as a special order. The lookup shows "GREASETUBE is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it." (S9-R16). If the part reached a line some other way, the system would refuse it with the same message (S9-R17).
New Line on S2-9647, picking the canned job "Replace - Steering shaft u joints", which includes GREASETUBE.
The line is added without GREASETUBE (S9-R9), and the user sees "GREASETUBE is inactive and was not added." The message stays until the user closes it (S9-R10).
The vendor return lookup includes inactive parts (S9-R11), because stock may still need to go back. The inactive one carries a grey "Inactive" tag beside its description (S9-R12).

Issue Credit on part sale P2-89 lists the parts sold, active or inactive. N79L-063 is now inactive and carries the grey "Inactive" tag beside its part number. Credits on work order invoices work the same way (S9-R13).

AN INACTIVE PART IN DAILY WORK

What a retired part does everywhere else: it is left out of new work, and kept where existing records still need it. GREASETUBE and N79L-063 are set inactive for these screens. Read left to right.

Board 6.0 is today's part lookup on a work order, traced from staging.
The page is called Catalog, and its New Catalog Part button creates entries that nothing points at.
Called Part Library in the side menu and the page title (Story 12). No control creates an entry (S11-R1). Search, filters, sorting, row selection and Set category stay (S11-R4, S11-R5).
Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3). New entries come only from a part number in use (S11-R6).

THE PART LIBRARY

The shared parts list is called the Part Library, and it is browse and edit only. Read left to right.

Board 7.0 is today's Catalog page, traced from staging.
